content:
Is there anywhere I can see why Reservoir thinks that a build failed? It says that a certain version doesn't build, but I'm a bit confused about what it chooses to try to build and why.

The most recent version mentioned on https://reservoir.lean-lang.org/@Timeroot/quantumInfo says that b7cf131 fails to build on v4.28, which makes sense because that commit was still on v4.24. While our most recent commit 9b74fd9, which is nearly a month old, doesn't seem to have been tried on any versions.

I just got rejected from a conference largely because (as far as I can tell) a reviewer looked at reservoir, saw that the code "didn't compile", and said that it should be rejected on those grounds. The code does compile of course (I just tested it on a fresh install) and the conference doesn't allow responses to reviewers. So I'm rather torn up about this.
Of course this isn't reservoir's fault, at all. I'd just like to figure out what more I can do in the future. :(
This is the conference reviewer's fault. It is worth raising this issue with the program chair.

I agree that it's their fault, and I'm consider raising it with the PC. But I doubt it will change anything in this case. (It's not a CS conference, I doubt they'll care that much, and decisions are generally final.)
Hovering over the 4.24.0 build, it says it failed with https://github.com/Timeroot/Lean-QuantumInfo/blob/410e7f2/lean-toolchain

Yes, that one was broken briefly, it was fixed later that day. Does Reservoir only run once per toolchain, is that the idea? That would be reasonable. (But still doesn't explain why it ran b7cf131 ran on the wrong version)
